subject: Pioneer Retail — LLM data use assurances & subprocessor mapping
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@pioneerretail.com>, procurement@pioneerretail.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pioneer Retail — LLM data use assurances & subprocessor mapping

Hi Alex / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. As a follow-up, Pioneer asked for operational evidence to support the no-training / model-improvement opt-out in the DPA and a clear map of subprocessors and data-export lanes (SFTP/API, KMS residency). To keep the review moving, I’ve summarized what we can share immediately and what we’ll need a short runbook to produce.

Quick summary (what we can provide now):
- Subprocessor inventory (CSV) with roles, datacenter region, and SOC2 status — attached.
- High-level ops proof that customer traffic is tagged and excluded from training pipelines (summary doc attached).
- Export options: SFTP export process and API export SLA; we can provide transient S3/SFTP evidence for pilot traffic.

Questions from Pioneer we should answer explicitly in the packet:
1) Can Redwood provide a timeline for generating a filtered export for a customer (SFTP + log of exported objects)?
2) Will Pioneer’s data ever be accessible to third-party subprocessors for model improvement work?
3) Can we attest to onshore key custody (KMS) for Pioneer if required?

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik, can you confirm the operational proof we can deliver within 5 business days and list anything that requires an ops run?
- David, please advise whether additional legal attestation language is required beyond our standard DPA addendum.
- Connor, please confirm expected lead time for a one-off full SFTP export and whether we can produce delivery logs.

I’ve attached our internal checklist to make the packet consistent with Pioneer’s template — this will also help procurement/Legal accept the DPA redlines faster.

Appreciate a quick read — Pioneer is hoping to close the pilot procurement by end of next week.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: redwood-no-train-evidence-checklist.pdf, subprocessor-inventory-20270323.csv

From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@pioneerretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@pioneerretail.com, Priya Singh <priya.s@pioneerretail.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pioneer Retail — LLM data use assurances & subprocessor mapping

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments — that helps. A few clarifying items from Legal / Procurement so we can scope the packet correctly:

1) Timeline for exports: procurement needs an operational SLA for one-off full exports (how long to produce and transfer).
2) Subprocessor granularity: the CSV is helpful — can you add a column that indicates whether each subprocessor can access request/response bodies (yes/no)?
3) KMS custodianship: was discussing onshore KMS with our security lead (Priya). If Redwood can offer customer-managed keys on a per-tenant basis, that would be ideal; otherwise we need an architectural diagram showing encryption and key access.

Also — we’ll share a short template with the exact evidence items we require (small checklist). Can Redwood provide a point-in-time export for a subset of pilot traffic as a proof-of-process? We do prefer SFTP delivery with checksums and a delivery log.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call Thursday to walk through the packet?

Best,
Alex
Senior Procurement Manager
Pioneer Retail
---
Attachments: Pioneer_evidence_template.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@pioneerretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pioneer Retail — LLM data use assurances & subprocessor mapping

Alex — thanks, and good clarifying questions. I’ll answer inline and note what requires a brief ops run:  

1) SLA for one-off exports: For pilot-scale tenant exports (<= 100GB), standard lead time is 48–72 hours to prepare and validate a full SFTP export with delivery logs and md5 checksums. For larger datasets we’ll provide a separate estimate. (Requires ops run to generate export zip and delivery log.)

2) CSV granularity: We can add the "access_to_bodies" column (yes/no) and a "purpose" field. I’ll attach an updated export after internal approval.

3) KMS / customer-managed keys (CMKs): Redwood supports CMK integration for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted pilots we can provide a hybrid option: onshore key wrapping + audit trail but not full CMK isolation by default. If Pioneer requires full CMK custody, we should discuss Dedicated capacity or a VPC Private control plane. I’ll include a short architecture sketch in the packet.

Proof-of-process for pilot traffic: Yes — we can run a one-off export of a subset and provide:
- SFTP delivery with checksums
- Delivery log (timestamped manifest of exported objects)
- Ops playbook excerpt that shows the export steps and approvals

What I need from Pioneer to proceed:
- Exact sample window (start/end timestamps) and sample tenant IDs
- Confirmation you’re comfortable with the 48–72 hour lead time for the pilot export

Connor, please flag any permissions or compliance gating that would push the lead time beyond 72 hours.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Compliance (contracts)
Redwood Inference

Hi all,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement reviewed Karthik’s timelines and we’re aligned on the 48–72 hour pilot export expectation. A couple of follow-ups before we confirm the call:

- Sample window: please export March 10–17, 2027 for tenant IDs PR-PILOT-01 and PR-PILOT-02.
- Subprocessor CSV: please include the access_to_bodies column and an admin contact for each subprocessor.
- Evidence delivery: SFTP to sftp.pioneerretail.com with md5 checksums and a delivery manifest. We will provide temporary SFTP credentials before the export.

If Redwood can push an updated CSV and a short architecture sketch for KMS by Wednesday EOD (our time), we’ll accept the DPA addendum and book the Thursday slot for a call to finalize operational handoffs.

We appreciate the responsiveness — small pilot so we want to move quickly.

Regards,

Priya Singh
Head of Security & Privacy
Pioneer Retail
